question: Do any of eight untried price-based signal families predict returns on the 2011-2026 panel, and does anything selected without seeing recent data still work recently?
why_these_eight: Every signal this project has tested is momentum, defensive/volatility, or fundamentals. These eight are the price-computable families it has not: a linkage-lite industry signal, three tail-risk moments, an instability measure, a dispersion measure, a bounce-controlled residual reversal, and a consistency measure. IndRetBig in particular sat in the OSAP screen's most-orthogonal band at 0.009 against every existing strategy and was never run.
owner_instruction: The owner asked to prioritise recent returns, reasoning that a strategy which won last decade may not work now. That reasoning is sound about regimes and dangerous as a selection rule, because selecting on recent returns in sample is how the four existing strategies came to correlate 0.72 to 0.97. The design below honours the instruction without the trap: signals are SELECTED on 2011-2019 and EVALUATED on 2020-2026, so 'does it work recently' is answered out of sample. What recent-window selection would have chosen is also reported, side by side, so the difference is visible rather than argued about.
data: data/clean_full_history_prices_v1/weekly_adjusted_prices_clean.csv.gz, 2,810 issuers, 817 weeks, corporate-action repaired in Step 240

declared_signals.ind_ret_big: lagged 4-week return of the largest-price quintile within the issuer's own sector, assigned to every member of that sector
declared_signals.coskewness: covariance of the issuer's return with the squared market return, 104-week window
declared_signals.downside_beta: beta estimated on weeks when the equal-weight market fell, 104-week window
declared_signals.idiosyncratic_skewness: third moment of the residual from a market regression, 104-week window
declared_signals.volatility_of_volatility: standard deviation of 13-week rolling volatility over 104 weeks
declared_signals.sector_dispersion: cross-sectional standard deviation of returns within the issuer's sector over 13 weeks
declared_signals.residual_reversal_skip1: minus the market-residual return over 4 weeks, skipping the most recent week to remove bid-ask bounce, the control that killed Step 250
declared_signals.trend_consistency: share of positive weeks over 26 weeks

windows.note: the evaluation window contains 2020, 2022 and the 2023-2026 bull, so it is not a single regime

controls.bounce: every signal uses a one-week skip between its last input and the forward return
controls.sign_declared: no sign is declared for these because none has an established direction here; a two-sided test is used and the sign found in selection must repeat in evaluation
controls.cost: 0, 10, 50 and 100 bps on the best surviving signal only
controls.correlation: against the four existing strategy paths; the point is breadth

interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_nothing_clears_in_selection: eight more families closed; record and move on
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_something_clears_in_selection_but_fli: that is the answer to the owner's question, and it is the expected one: a signal that worked last decade and not now
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.if_something_clears_in_selection_and_rep: a genuine candidate, and the first signal in this project selected without seeing the window it is judged on
interpretation_fixed_in_advance.always: a cross-sectional IC is not a strategy. Anything surviving still needs a book, costs, concentration and a forward clock.

cumulative_trial_warning: These 8 stack on every configuration searched across 255 recorded steps.
